title: Handoff snipe scratch — quick review + followups
content:
Context:
Small post-handoff scratchpad for quick "snipe" style reviews — things I want to catch fast after a handoff so ops & SRE don't get paged. Not comprehensive; prioritize reproducible gaps, safety, perf, and rollout strategy.

PR under look: #4310 - "kv-cache: graceful degrade on OOM during batch insert"
Author: Evan Z. (paired w/ infra on the autoscaler behavior)
Why this feels risky: changes the eviction timing and also adds a fallback path that proxies requests to a cold path. Potentially increases P95 tail if fallback triggers frequently.

Quick checklist (do first):
- [ ] Sanity: confirm API contract unchanged (inputs/outputs, error codes). Search for uses of kv-insert that assume success.
- [ ] Tests: unit + integration present? See PR for unit tests but no streaming integration test that simulates high token length inflight. Add small reproducer.
- [ ] Metrics: ensure new code emits a clear metric (kv.cache.fallback.count) and tags (model, route, region). If not, add before merge.
- [ ] Rollout plan: prefer canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with auto-rollback on error-rate > 1% relative. Add flag gate.
- [ ] Backwards compatibility: verify older model variants with different kv layouts still behave. Put a short checklist in PR description.
- [ ] Observability: add log line for fallback path including trace id and reason (OOM / quota). Keep logs rate-limited.

Refactor ideas (future follow-ups):
- Move eviction heuristics into a strategy registry (simple interface: shouldEvict(batch) -> reason). Right now heuristics are spread across codepaths.
- Introduce a synthetic-load integration test harness that can run locally in CI using a tiny model shim to exercise long-sequence KV growth. Cheap to run (30s).
- Extract metric-tag enrichment into a middleware so metrics for fallback/cold-path always carry request route/model/context.

Small code notes found while scanning:
- In cache_manager.go: the comment says "evict after n inserts" but implementation uses elapsed time micro-buckets. Suggest aligning variable names and comment.
- Inline retry logic in batch_executor looks duplicated with stream_executor.retry; factor to shared util.
- Potential off-by-one in recent change: when computing maxCapacity - currentSize, ensure we don't drop to zero and then treat as success.

Testing to add now (quick and mailable):
- Reproducer script: python repro_kv_fallback.py --batch-size 128 --seq-len 8192
- Unit: assert that when kv insert triggers fallback, the original request returns 202 + "fallback" tag (or whatever contract we choose). Prefer deterministic behavior in unit vs integration.
- Integration: run small dockerized runtime with mocked GPU shim, send 500 concurrent short/long requests to validate fallback triggers and metrics.

Follow-ups & owners (tentative):
- Add metric + tags: Mira (0.5d)
- Canary rollout config + feature flag: SRE (Patrick) + myself for runbook (1d)
- Add local repro + CI harness: Evan (1d)
- Minor refactors (strategy registry + shared retry util): backlog, schedule in next sprint (2-3d)

Open questions (need answers before final merge):
1) What should the client-visible behavior be on fallback? Current PR returns a soft-success with a header "x-kv-fallback: true" — is that acceptable for downstream callers? (Product input?)
2) Do we want to expose a per-tenant cap to avoid noisy neighbors triggering fallbacks globally? (ops cost/complexity)
3) Is the metric cardinality acceptable as-is? We need to ensure we don't blow up metric ingestion by adding too high-cardinality tags.

Notes to self (quick):
- Ping @mira in Slack for metric naming convention.
- Add a short blurb to PR description about expected perf delta (local bench numbers: P95 +8-12ms under one run). Document methodology.
- If fallback rate > 0.5% during canary, abort and revert change.

One-liners for reviewers to scan (put in PR header):
- "Adds graceful fallback on kv-insert OOM to preserve latency SLOs at cost of cold-path token compute. Emits kv.cache.fallback metric and feature-flag guarded rollout."
- "Suggested canary: 5% (24h) -> 25% (24h) -> 100% with rollback on +1% error-rate or +50% fallback-rate relative to baseline."

Tidbits / heuristics I used while reviewing:
- Always look for metrics + tags first — if we can't measure it, don't deploy it.
- If behavior is opt-in via flag, prefer a conservative default (off) for anything that changes memory handling.
- Prefer small, isolated refactors post-merge instead of big structural moves in the same PR that touches rollback surface.

If I get 30m: add the two small unit tests and a short canary runbook into the PR template. If I don't get to it, leave clear TODOs in PR and assign owners above.

---
End scratchpad. Will prune and move concrete items into the PR description and a follow-up ticket in INF board.
